findings.explanation: The repository's Splunkbase catalog lists Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server as app 2648; 2926 is not that add-on. The same wrong ID is repeated in detailedImplementation and in the references title.
findings.quote: Optional Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server ([Splunkbase 2926](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/2926))
findings.suggested_fix: Change to Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server ([Splunkbase 2648](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/2648)) in app, detailedImplementation and references.

findings.explanation: The reference points at the Splunkbase home page rather than the add-on page, so it does not support the claim it is attached to. The EEOC reference likewise points at the generic /employers/ landing page instead of the EEO-1 Component 1 page.
findings.suggested_fix: Use https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/2648 for the SQL Server add-on, and the EEOC EEO-1 data collection page for the EEO-1 reference.

findings.explanation: dataSources, app and implementation route gender/ethnicity data into `business` (24-month retention, revops/fp_a/executive roles), but the category guide's role-separation table puts special-category diversity data in `hr_diversity` (3 named users, 13 months). `hr_analytics` does not exist in the guide either.
findings.quote: Primary aggregate snapshots land in `index=business` (or a restricted `index=hr_analytics` if governance splits people data).
findings.suggested_fix: Land raw demographic pulls in `index=hr_diversity` restricted to hr_diversity_view, with 13-month retention, and only push suppressed aggregates to wider indexes or lookups. Update dataSources, app, implementation and detailedImplementation Step 1 to match.

findings.explanation: A second, generic Steps 1–5 block is appended after the bespoke guide. It contradicts the UC: the SPL reads lookups, so time windows, index=main, tstats/timechart gap checks and paging the platform on-call do not apply, and paging on-call with diversity data clashes with the HR Legal–only routing in implementation.
findings.quote: Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=see SPL into index=main. ... Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. ... Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the entire second 'Step 1 — Configure data collection' to 'Step 5 — Troubleshooting' block and keep the bespoke Steps 1–5.

findings.explanation: All four entries are template placeholders (target_index, configured_sourcetype, span=1h, synthetic probes) that cannot occur in a nightly lookup-based representation report. The real causes of misleading status flags are already listed in detailedImplementation Step 5.
findings.quote: Maintenance window on `target_index` (UC-23.4.3)** — Planned work for 'Diversity and Inclusion Metrics Dashboard' shifts `headcount`, `level_total` over `span=1h`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with real causes: self-ID campaign refresh jumps, small-population swings after one departure, M&A denominator inflation, job-grade renames that break the role_level mapping, and annual promotion-cycle stair-steps. Each should come with its mitigation (annotation, trailing-quarter smoothing, freeze YoY).

findings.explanation: These specific opt-out and disclosure rates have no source, and they read as authoritative benchmarks that operators may use to judge their own data.
findings.quote: blending US (~8%), EU (~18% post GDPR), and UK (~12%) cohorts ... Schedule A disability disclosure rates hovering near five percent ... VEVRAA veteran self-ID percentages (~7–8%)
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a source for each figure (e.g., OFCCP Section 503 7% utilization goal, VEVRAA hiring benchmark), or reword as 'compare against your own historical disclosure rate' without numbers.

findings.explanation: Workday's public REST API is normally addressed as `/ccx/api/v1/{tenant}/workers`, which is the pattern sibling UC-23.4.6 uses. `/workday-rest/v1/workers` does not appear to be a documented path.
findings.suggested_fix: Check against Workday REST API documentation and align with the `/ccx/api/v1/{tenant}/workers` form used elsewhere in the subcategory.

findings.explanation: Dashboard Studio has no native funnel visualization. A level-ordered bar chart or a custom visualization would be needed, and the text does not say so.
findings.quote: Funnel or cascade visuals from Individual Contributor — Junior through C-Suite
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'a level-ordered horizontal bar chart (or a Splunkbase funnel custom visualization)' so readers know a native panel does not exist.

findings.explanation: Oracle Database is only one optional replica path (EBS via DB Connect). Tagging it as the sole equipment model, with no Workday/SuccessFactors/SQL Server equivalent, overstates its role and ignores the `mssql` equipment tag.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop equipmentModels or add matching models for the other listed sources, such as the SQL Server path.

findings.explanation: The UC is marked verified even though the app ID is wrong, half of detailedImplementation is generic template text, and knownFalsePositives, description, value, evidence and controlTest are placeholder skeletons.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or community until the app ID, index governance and template residue are fixed and re-reviewed.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: Small-cell suppression is defeatable: `where headcount >= 5` runs after `level_total` and `representation_pct` are computed, so the remaining rows' headcounts and percentages let a reader subtract their way back to the hidden cell's count (complementary disclosure). Suppression should also remove or recompute the level totals, or apply secondary suppression.

`coalesce(gender, "Prefer not to say")` merges missing or never-collected data with employees who actively declined. That inflates the declined cohort and hides ingestion gaps. Use a separate 'Not recorded' bucket.
`ethnicity_normalized` is computed but never used by the stats, so the ethnicity breakdown promised in visualization and the grandma text is not produced by this search.

`join type=outer` with the diversity_targets subsearch adds target rows for suppressed or absent cells with null headcount and representation_pct. `gap_vs_goal` then evaluates to null and status_flag falls through to 'No goal set', which is misleading. Use `lookup diversity_targets.csv role_level gender_normalized OUTPUT target_pct AS goal_pct` instead.

summary: The hand-written parts (dataSources, implementation, the first Steps 1–5 troubleshooting list) are rich and domain-aware, but the UC cites the wrong Splunkbase ID for the SQL Server add-on, lands special-category data outside the guide's restricted hr_diversity index, and carries a pasted generic template (second Steps 1–5, placeholder knownFalsePositives) that contradicts the lookup-based design.
